Disaster recovery, quotas, automation, visibility, legacy workloads and the design check

html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. AZ: Availability Zone; RPO: recovery point objective; RTO: recovery time objective; NAT: network address translation; SQS: Simple Queue Service; TTL: time to live; RDS: Relational Database Service; DB: database; IAM: Identity and Access Management; EBS: Elastic Block Store; EFS: Elastic File System; AMI: Amazon Machine Image; CI: continuous integration; CD: continuous delivery; MGN: Application Migration Service; AI: artificial intelligence; DR: disaster recovery; EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud

  • Design for high availability and fault tolerance across AZs and Regions
  • Remove single points of failure and choose failover and routing approaches
  • Select a disaster recovery strategy from RPO and RTO
  • Use automation and immutable infrastructure, and manage quotas and throttling
  • Pick services for visibility and for legacy and non-cloud workloads

2Availability, failure domains, routing and data tier

Running case

Lantern and Loom Survives a Bad Day

  • A power event in one zone took the whole shop offline for 40 minutes
  • Leaders now ask: what if a whole Region fails?
  • Targets: lose at most minutes of data, recover in about an hour
  • An old inventory server cannot be changed
  • Your job: choose the redundancy, failover and recovery design

High Availability, Fault Tolerance and Resilience

Term Meaning
High availability The workload keeps serving with minimal interruption when a component fails, using redundancy and fast failover
Fault tolerance The workload keeps running without interruption through a failure; higher cost and complexity
Resilience The ability to recover from disruption and keep meeting demand
  • Availability is a percent of time: 99.9% allows about 8.8 hours of downtime a year, 99.99% about 53 minutes, 99.999% about 5 minutes
  • Set targets from business requirements
Exam tip

Each extra nine costs more; choose the availability the business actually needs.

Removing Single Points of Failure

  • A load balancer and an Auto Scaling group that span two or more Availability Zones (AZs)
  • One NAT gateway per AZ; a Multi-AZ database
  • Each zone's route table sends traffic to its own NAT gateway
  • S3, DynamoDB and SQS already run across zones
  • Hunt for singles: one instance, one AZ, one DNS record, one manual step

Exam tip

If one thing failing takes the workload down, it is a single point of failure.

Multi-AZ or Multi-Region?

Multi-AZ Multi-Region
Protects against A data center or zone failure A whole Region failure
Distance AZs are far enough apart to avoid shared failures, close enough for synchronous replication Far apart: replication is asynchronous
Also gives The default high availability Compliance distance, lower latency for global users
Cost and effort Moderate Higher
Exam tip

A zone-level failure needs Multi-AZ; a Region-level disaster or a distance rule needs Multi-Region.

Failover Patterns and Health Checks

  • Active-passive: a standby takes traffic only after a failure; active-active: every site serves traffic
  • Health checks detect failures; load balancers, Auto Scaling and Route 53 act on them
  • Automatic failover can trigger on false alarms; many teams use manual start with automated steps
  • Rely on the data plane during failover, not control plane changes
  • Distributed patterns: timeouts, retries with backoff, queues, stateless services, idempotent work
Exam tip

Pre-provision what recovery needs, so failover does not depend on creating resources during the outage.

Amazon Route 53 Routing Policies

Policy Use it to
Simple Serve one resource for a domain
Failover Set up active-passive failover
Latency Send users to the Region with the best latency
Weighted Split traffic in set proportions
Geolocation Route by the user's location
Geoproximity Route by resource location, with an optional shift
IP-based Route by the user's IP address range
Multivalue answer Return up to eight healthy records at random
Exam tip

Backup site: failover. Fastest Region: latency. Gradual rollout: weighted.

Route 53 Health Checks and DNS Failover

  • Failover records: a primary and a secondary, with a health check on the primary
  • When the check fails, Route 53 answers with the secondary
  • Alias records can evaluate target health for AWS resources
  • DNS caching and the TTL delay a switch; Global Accelerator uses static IP addresses and avoids DNS caching

Exam tip

Automatic DNS failover to a standby Region: Route 53 failover routing with health checks.

Database High Availability

Option What it gives
RDS Multi-AZ DB instance One synchronous standby in another AZ and automatic failover; the standby does not serve reads
RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster Two readable standbys
Aurora Storage copied across three AZs; replicas can take over
Aurora Global Database Cross-Region replication, typical lag under a second, promote a secondary in under a minute
DynamoDB global tables Multi-Region reads and writes, last writer wins
Exam tip

Survive a zone failure: Multi-AZ. Survive a Region failure: Aurora Global Database or global tables.

Amazon RDS Proxy

  • A managed proxy that pools and shares database connections
  • Makes applications more resilient to database failures: it connects to a standby while preserving application connections
  • Absorbs surges and queues or throttles connections the database cannot serve yet
  • Supports IAM authentication and Secrets Manager credentials
  • Works for most applications with no code changes
  • A strong fit for Lambda, which opens many short connections
Exam tip

Connection storms or slow failover reconnects: RDS Proxy.

Storage Durability and Availability

  • Durability means data is not lost; availability means you can reach it
  • S3 stores data across multiple AZs and is designed for eleven nines of durability
  • An EBS volume is replicated inside one AZ: use snapshots to protect it across zones and Regions
  • EFS is Regional, stored across zones
  • Replicate to another Region with S3 replication, snapshot copies and AWS Backup
  • Turn on S3 Versioning to undo mistaken deletes
Exam tip

Block storage lives in one zone: protect it with snapshots; object storage spans zones by default.

3Disaster recovery, quotas, automation, visibility, legacy workloads and the design check

RPO and RTO

  • RPO (recovery point objective): how much data loss, measured in time, is acceptable
  • RTO (recovery time objective): how long the service may be down
  • Backup or replication frequency sets the RPO; the recovery process sets the RTO
  • Both come from business requirements, and tighter targets cost more

Exam tip

RPO looks back at lost data; RTO looks forward at downtime.

Four Disaster Recovery Strategies

  • Backup and restore: copy data to the recovery Region; redeploy everything after a disaster
  • Pilot light: data replicated continuously; core infrastructure ready; app servers switched off
  • Warm standby: a scaled-down but running copy that can take traffic at once
  • Multi-site active/active: full capacity in several Regions serving users

Exam tip

The more you keep running in the recovery Region, the faster and costlier the recovery.

Comparing the Strategies

Strategy Running in the recovery Region Typical recovery Cost
Backup and restore Only backups Hours Lowest
Pilot light Data stores only Tens of minutes Low
Warm standby A scaled-down full stack Minutes Medium
Active/active A full-size stack Near zero Highest
  • Pilot light cannot take requests until you turn on servers; warm standby can, at reduced capacity
  • Hot standby is a full-size copy that serves no traffic until needed
Exam tip

Read the RTO and RPO, then pick the cheapest strategy that still meets both.

Building the Recovery Region

  • Replicate data: S3 replication, RDS read replicas, Aurora Global Database, DynamoDB global tables
  • Switch traffic: Route 53 health checks, Global Accelerator, or CloudFront origin failover
  • Promote the replica and scale out the application with Auto Scaling in the recovery Region
  • Redeploy infrastructure with infrastructure as code
  • Keep service quotas high enough in the recovery Region
  • Test failover regularly; AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery replicates servers using pilot light
Exam tip

A recovery plan you have not tested is a guess.

Service Quotas and Throttling

  • Service Quotas shows your quotas from one place and lets you request increases
  • Quotas are set per account and per Region; some are adjustable, some fixed
  • A standby Region needs the same quotas as production, or scale-out at failover will fail
  • Monitor utilization and set alarms before you reach a limit
  • Throttling returns errors when you exceed a rate: use retries with exponential backoff and jitter
  • Services such as API Gateway and Lambda also throttle requests
Exam tip

Raise quotas in the recovery Region before the disaster, not during it.

Automation and Immutable Infrastructure

  • Infrastructure as code: CloudFormation describes resources in a template and builds the same stack repeatedly, in many Regions
  • Immutable infrastructure: replace servers from a new golden AMI instead of patching them
  • Auto Scaling replaces unhealthy instances automatically
  • Systems Manager automates patching and operations; Service Catalog offers approved products
  • Templates in version control make changes trackable and reversible
  • Clicks in the Management Console do not repeat; templates and scripts do
Exam tip

Repeatable, identical environments in another Region: CloudFormation. Replace, do not patch: immutable.

Systems Manager, Service Catalog, Proton and the Well-Architected Tool [Verify live]

Service What it does
Systems Manager Manage nodes at scale: patching, Session Manager, Run Command, Automation, Parameter Store, no bastion hosts
Service Catalog A catalog of approved products, with constraints, for self-service launch
AWS Proton Templates for standard application stacks and CI/CD
Well-Architected Tool Review a workload against the framework's pillars and get an improvement plan
  • As of 5 November 2026: the docs announce Proton end of support on 7 October 2026; check its status
Exam tip

Operate fleets: Systems Manager. Approved self-service products: Service Catalog.

Workload Visibility: X-Ray, Health and Grafana

Service What it shows
AWS X-Ray Traces of requests through your services and a service map to find bottlenecks and errors
AWS Health Dashboard AWS service events and events that affect your resources; events also reach EventBridge
Amazon Managed Grafana Dashboards over CloudWatch, X-Ray and other data sources
Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus Prometheus-compatible metrics, especially for containers
  • Metrics, logs and alarms in CloudWatch come in module 7
Exam tip

Which downstream call is slow or failing? X-Ray. Is AWS having a problem? Health Dashboard.

Improving Reliability of Legacy Applications Old name [Verify live]

  • AWS Application Migration Service (the docs now call it AWS Transform MGN) rehosts servers with continuous block-level replication and short cutovers, with no application changes
  • AWS Application Discovery Service collects server usage and dependencies for planning
  • RDS Proxy, load balancers and Route 53 add resilience without code changes
  • Elastic Disaster Recovery protects servers without changing them
  • VMware Cloud on AWS runs existing VMware workloads unchanged on AWS
  • As of 5 November 2026: Application Discovery Service is closed to new customers; check the page
Exam tip

When the application cannot change, add resilience around it: rehost, proxy, balance and replicate.

Purpose-Built AWS AI Services

Service Use it for
Amazon Comprehend Sentiment, entities and key phrases in text
Amazon Polly Text to lifelike speech
Amazon Transcribe Speech to text
Amazon Translate Language translation
Amazon Rekognition Objects, faces and unsafe content in images and video
Amazon Textract Text, forms and tables from scanned documents
Amazon Lex Chatbots for voice and text
Amazon SageMaker AI Build, train and deploy your own models
Exam tip

A ready-made API beats running your own models: less to operate and built to scale.

What the Exam Asks: High Availability and Recovery

  • Which redundancy: Multi-AZ, Multi-Region, Auto Scaling or a Multi-AZ database
  • Which routing or failover: Route 53 policy, health check or Global Accelerator
  • Which DR strategy: from RPO, RTO and cost
  • Which automation: CloudFormation, Systems Manager or Service Catalog
  • Which visibility or legacy tool: X-Ray, Health, RDS Proxy or Application Migration Service
Exam tip

Match the failure size to the fix: instance, zone, Region or data corruption.

Design Check: Lantern and Loom Survives a Bad Day

Requirement Design
Survive the loss of a zone Auto Scaling across two AZs, a load balancer, Multi-AZ RDS
Database failover without code changes RDS Multi-AZ, with RDS Proxy for connections
Region disaster, an hour to recover, minutes of data loss Pilot light: replicated data, switched-off servers
Switch users to the other Region automatically Route 53 failover with health checks
Rebuild the stack identically elsewhere CloudFormation templates
Make sure scale-out works at failover Raise Service Quotas in the recovery Region
Find the slow downstream call AWS X-Ray
The old inventory server cannot change Application Migration Service
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1What does a recovery point objective (RPO) of 15 minutes mean for Lantern and Loom's order data?

  • AThe service must be running again within 15 minutes of a failure
  • BNo more than 15 minutes of order data may be lost
  • CBackups must be kept for 15 minutes before they are deleted
  • DFailover must be tested every 15 minutes
Show the answer

Answer: B. RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time. The time to restore service is the recovery time objective (RTO).

S2Lantern and Loom runs one EC2 instance and one single-AZ RDS database in the same Availability Zone. Which TWO changes let the shop survive the loss of that zone? (Select TWO.)

  • ARun the web tier in an Auto Scaling group across two zones behind a load balancer
  • BReplace the instance with a larger instance type
  • CConvert the database to a Multi-AZ deployment
  • DTake a manual snapshot of the database each night
  • EAttach an Elastic IP address to the instance
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Spreading servers across zones behind a load balancer and giving the database a standby in another zone removes both single points of failure. A larger instance, nightly snapshots and an Elastic IP address all stay in the failed zone or recover slowly.

S3Lantern and Loom wants product pages read aloud for visually impaired shoppers, and wants the sentiment of reviews flagged, with the least operational effort. Which services fit?

  • ATwo custom models trained and hosted on Amazon SageMaker AI
  • BAmazon Rekognition and Amazon Textract
  • CAmazon Polly for speech and Amazon Comprehend for sentiment analysis
  • DAmazon Lex and Amazon Transcribe
Show the answer

Answer: C. Polly turns text into speech and Comprehend detects sentiment in text, and both are ready-made services with nothing to train or run. Rekognition and Textract read images and documents, and Lex and Transcribe handle chatbots and speech to text.

S4If a whole Region fails, Lantern and Loom accepts about an hour to recover and a few minutes of data loss, and wants the lowest running cost that still meets this. Which strategy fits?

  • APilot light: replicate the data and keep servers switched off
  • BBackup and restore from nightly backups copied to a second Region
  • CMulti-site active/active with full capacity in two Regions
  • DWarm standby with a scaled-down copy that serves traffic
Show the answer

Answer: A. Pilot light keeps data replicated continuously, which meets the few-minutes RPO, and turning on servers fits an hour of recovery at low cost. Nightly backups miss the RPO, and the other two cost more than needed.

S5The order database must survive the loss of its Availability Zone, with automatic failover and no application changes. Reads can stay on the primary. Which RDS configuration fits?

  • AA read replica in the same Availability Zone
  • BA cross-Region read replica that is promoted by hand
  • CDaily automated backups only
  • DA Multi-AZ DB instance deployment
Show the answer

Answer: D. A Multi-AZ DB instance deployment keeps a synchronous standby in another zone and fails over automatically through the same endpoint. A replica in the same zone does not help, and a cross-Region replica or backups need manual recovery.

S6Many Lambda functions open database connections that exhaust an RDS database, and failovers disrupt the functions. What should the architect add?

  • AMore memory and a longer timeout for each Lambda function
  • BA read replica for every function
  • CAmazon ElastiCache for every query
  • DAmazon RDS Proxy in front of the database
Show the answer

Answer: D. RDS Proxy pools and shares connections and reconnects to the standby during a failover while preserving application connections. More memory, replicas or a cache do not manage connections.

S7Which TWO statements about Amazon Route 53 routing policies are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • AFailover routing sets up active-passive failover
  • BGeolocation routing sends users to the Region with the lowest latency
  • CLatency routing sends users to the Region that gives the best latency
  • DWeighted routing can send traffic to only one resource
  • ESimple routing is the policy for active-passive failover
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Failover routing is active-passive, and latency routing picks the Region with the best latency. Geolocation routes by user location, weighted routing splits traffic in proportions, and simple routing serves a single resource.

S8After a disaster, Lantern and Loom must recreate its whole environment, including network, load balancers and servers, in a second Region quickly and identically. What is the best approach?

  • AFollow a written runbook that engineers carry out step by step in the console
  • BKeep screenshots of every console setting for the engineers to follow
  • CDefine it in CloudFormation templates and deploy them to the second Region
  • DKeep one golden server image and rebuild the rest of the stack by hand
Show the answer

Answer: C. Infrastructure as code recreates identical resources repeatedly in any Region. Runbooks, screenshots and a lone image leave manual steps that are slow and error-prone.

S9An aging inventory application runs on a physical server in the warehouse and cannot be changed. Lantern and Loom wants to move it to AWS with minimal downtime. Which service fits?

  • AAWS Application Migration Service
  • BAWS Service Catalog, to publish an approved product
  • CAWS Proton, to template the server's deployment pipeline
  • DAWS Health Dashboard, to monitor the move
Show the answer

Answer: A. Application Migration Service rehosts servers with continuous block-level replication and a short cutover, with no application changes. The documentation now calls it AWS Transform MGN. Service Catalog, Proton and the Health Dashboard do not migrate servers.

S10Requests to Lantern and Loom's API pass through API Gateway, Lambda and DynamoDB, and some are slow. Which service shows a service map and request traces to find the slow component?

  • AAWS Config
  • BAWS X-Ray
  • CAWS Health Dashboard
  • DAWS Service Catalog
Show the answer

Answer: B. X-Ray collects traces of requests across services and draws a service map that points to bottlenecks and errors. Config records configuration, the Health Dashboard reports AWS events, and Service Catalog offers approved products.
